tagline: Flowers for weddings that look like the season they are in
intro: A Cotswold studio making loose, garden-led flowers for weddings and gatherings, grown here or within a morning's drive.
trust_line: Wedding and event florist, the Cotswolds
about_title: A cutting garden, a barn and a very full diary
about:
Clara Rye left a career in publishing to grow flowers in a walled garden outside Stow-on-the-Wold. The studio now takes on twenty weddings a year, so that each one has her full attention.

We work with what the season offers: blossom and tulips in spring, roses and sweet peas in June, dahlias and grasses in autumn. Nothing is flown in and nothing is arranged in foam.

services.name: Full wedding flowers
services.description: Ceremony, reception and everything carried or worn, designed around your venue and month.

services.name: Bridal party only
services.description: Bouquets, buttonholes and flower crowns for smaller celebrations.

services.name: Installations
services.description: Arches, hanging clouds and staircases built on site the day before.

services.name: Supper clubs and events
services.description: Table flowers for private dinners, launches and editorial shoots.

services.name: Buckets of flowers
services.description: Seasonal stems by the bucket for those arranging their own.

services.name: Workshops
services.description: A morning in the garden learning to arrange a hand-tied bouquet.

values.title: In season, always
values.text: Your flowers reflect the month you marry in, not a photograph from another one.

values.title: Grown, not flown
values.text: Nine in ten stems are cut within fifty miles of the studio.

values.title: Foam free
values.text: Everything is arranged in water, moss and reusable frames.

process.title: A conversation
process.text: We talk about your venue, your month and the feeling you want in the room.

process.title: A proposal
process.text: A written design with a palette, a list of likely flowers and a clear price.

process.title: A walk through
process.text: We visit the venue together six weeks before to settle every detail.

process.title: The day itself
process.text: We arrive early, stay until everything is right and return to clear.

faq.q: How far ahead should we book?
faq.a: Most couples book nine to fourteen months ahead. We take one wedding a weekend.
We agree a palette and a mood, then choose the best of what is flowering that week. It always looks better.
Yes, within about ninety minutes of Stow-on-the-Wold. Further by arrangement.

faq.q: What happens to the flowers afterwards?
faq.a: Guests are encouraged to take them home. Anything left goes to a local hospice.

projects.title: Isobel and Hugh
projects.summary: Roses, foxgloves and sweet peas down a forty-foot table.
projects.details: A June wedding in a walled garden. The ceremony arch was moved to the marquee by six ushers and a wheelbarrow.

projects.title: Amara and Jon
projects.summary: Dahlias, rosehips and copper beech in a barn lit by candles.
projects.details: Three hundred stems of dahlia cut the morning before, in a palette of plum and rust.

projects.title: A spring elopement
projects.summary: One bouquet, one buttonhole and a doorway of blossom.
projects.details: Twelve guests, a church porch and branches cut from the orchard at dawn.

projects.title: Midwinter supper
projects.summary: Hellebores, paperwhites and bare branches for a dinner of sixty.
projects.details: Planted bowls that guests took home at the end of the night.
